name: code-slots

frames.best_why: All six slots are filled with the digits 428193, showing the complete code entry state.

tagline: Six code boxes that spring each digit in, then flash a tick on success.
summary: A one-time code field split into individual rounded slots. Digits spring into place as you type or paste, the caret follows along, and a full code can show a success wash with a tick or drain away on error.
appearance: A rounded dark card with a heading, a line naming the email address, and six rounded square slots in a row. Filled slots turn pale with dark digits, the active one glows, and a small resend line sits below.
behaviour: Typing a digit drops it into the current slot with a spring and moves the caret forward; pasting fills every remaining slot. A correct code opens into a white bar with a tick, while a wrong one drains the digits back out.
demo_content: Heading "Check your inbox", the address maya@stashui.dev and the code 428193.
search_phrases: paste a code into separate boxes
use_when: A sign-in or two-factor screen needs a short numeric code entered quickly, including paste and SMS autofill.
avoid_when: It only accepts digits at a fixed length, and the fixed slot sizes make it awkward in very narrow cards.
customise: Props set length, controlled value, change and complete callbacks, status, masking, autofocus, colours, slot size, gap, radius and spring tuning.
weight_why: Six slots with short spring animations; only the caret blinks on a loop.

a11y.note: Typing, paste and arrow keys all work and progress is announced, but the field shows no focus ring beyond the blinking caret.

issues: The only focus cue is a thin caret; the hidden input itself has no outline.
polish_why: Crisp OTP flow with a satisfying spring and clear success state; small muted supporting text.
